x: Pairing file needed The pairing file lets Porthole switch JIT on, which games need to run at speed. Without it the game cannot start.

n: The tunnel says "connecting" and then "disconnected" after an update
x: [tunnel] ... connecting, then disconnected iOS sometimes keeps old information about the app's helper after an update.

n: "Large address space is not allowed" in the install check
x: [install] note: Large address space is not allowed This copy of Porthole was signed without the permission that lets games map the big block of address space the engine reserves for them. Some games will not start, or close shortly after they do. Many games run fine without it, so the line is a note, not always a fault.

n: "Steam did not accept the saved sign-in for downloads"
x: Steam: the sign-in for downloads was refused (result 5).  [cloud] skipped: Steam did not accept the saved sign-in for downloads. Sign in for downloads again. The sign-in Porthole saved for downloads and Steam Cloud has expired or was refused, so cloud saves are skipped for that run. The game itself can still start.

n: Steam sign-in or downloads fail on one network only
x: TLS or connection errors to Steam Some work and school networks block Steam.

n: "Minimum required feature level D3D_FEATURE_LEVEL_12_0 not supported"
x: Maximum supported feature level: D3D_FEATURE_LEVEL_11_1  /  Minimum required feature level D3D_FEATURE_LEVEL_12_0 not supported The game's Direct3D 11 mode asks for feature level 12_0, and Porthole's Direct3D 11 layer reports 11_1 at most. The game then shows its own error and closes. A setting cannot raise that level.

n: Black screen and 0 FPS after the game ran well for a while (DirectX 12)
x: Queue::Wait: fence ... never reached N in 5 s (at 0); continuing A command queue is waiting for a fence that nothing ever signalled, so the game stops drawing frames. The process is still alive: sound may carry on. One known cause is a game that writes a marker value with WriteBufferImmediate and then waits for it (see the next entry).

[madeira-d3d12] unimplemented: ID3D12GraphicsCommandList7::WriteBufferImmediate The game called a Direct3D 12 function that writes a small value from the GPU. By default Porthole ignores it, because writing it is switched off. A game that waits for that value will wait forever.

[mem-pressure] CRITICAL: app 6723 MB, free 1469 MB, gpu 4536 MB Porthole is close to the memory iOS lets one app use. The game may stutter, freeze, or be closed by iOS without warning. The numbers say how much the app, the free memory and the graphics memory are using.
